flags.text: No evidence was supplied for this objective: no caution boxes, no worked-example remarks, no independent re-solve wrong turns, no wrong options or widget predicates, and no existing entries. Every question listed is a worked example with a canonical solution and none has a distractor. I found no honest basis for a catalogue entry, so I wrote none. Any entry (for example 'one pair of equal or parallel opposite sides is enough') would be an error I assumed in general, not one the evidence supports, so the runtime falls back to the canonical solutions.

The canonical solutions for the worked examples with the bisector figures (we01, ex12-1-8, ex12-2-10), the two 'redraw the diagram' examples (ex12-1-9, ex12-2-11) are unusable as refutation material: ex12-1-8 is only a figure, and the 'redraw' ones give no worked argument. I did not use them.

Two canonical solutions look inconsistent with their stems and I did not build on them. ex12-1-6a gives both pairs of opposite sides parallel but concludes by 'opp. sides of quad are =' after proving congruent triangles. ex12-2-1 ends with 'AM=MO=ON=NO', which looks like a typo for AM=MO=ON=NA. Both need human review.

The objective description lists three criteria: opposite angles equal, opposite sides parallel, diagonals bisect each other. The canonical solutions also use 'two sides are parallel and equal' (ex12-1-1b) and 'one pair opp sides equal and parallel' (ex12-2-2c) as a criterion for a parallelogram, and 'both pairs of opposite sides equal' (ex12-1-6a). Check that the book treats these as taught criteria before any entry relies on them.

The book's reason wording is abbreviated: 'co-int angles', 'alt angles', 'opp sides of quad ∥', 'Midpt Theorem', 'opp sides parm eq', 'diagonals bisect each other', 'vert opp angles =', 'angles opp equal sides'. I did not use any of these terms in student-facing text, since I wrote no entries.

No evidence was supplied for this objective: no caution boxes, no worked-example remarks, no wrong turns from the independent re-solve, and no wrong options or widget predicates (no D0, D1, ...). Nothing the brief allows me to cite supports a diagnosable error, so I wrote no entries rather than invent one from general teaching experience. The runtime falls back to the canonical solutions for this objective, which is the stated safe default. A reasonable error to watch for in live use, if a later pass gets evidence for it, is a student treating opposite angles of a parallelogram as supplementary (using 180 minus the given angle where the book simply equates the opposite angle). I did not write it up because nothing here evidences it.

Data problem for human review, q:g10m12s1-1-2:ex12-2-7c: the recorded working reads x = 180 - 63 - 79 = 79, but 180 - 63 - 79 = 38. The stated answer (79) disagrees with the working's own arithmetic. The question has no figure here, so I could not tell which angle x is. Do not build any catalogue entry, or any grading predicate, on this question until the answer and working are reconciled.

Data problem for human review, expl:g10m12s1-1-2:ex12-2-13: the canonical working lists BC = EF and BC = AD, then concludes EF = ED. Those two lines give EF = AD, not EF = ED. The later lines (AD + DE = AE, EF + DE = DF, DE common) only work with EF = AD. This looks like a transcription slip. I did not use it.

Unusable canonical solutions: expl:g10m12s1-1-2:ex12-2-3a, ex12-2-4a and ex12-2-12c carry only 'First number the angles' (figure-only) or 'proved above', so they contain no method to argue against or from. Questions ex12-1-6b and ex12-1-6c lean on a part 'proved above' that is not in this pool, so they are not self-contained either.

Objective scope for review: a large share of this objective's questions are about the Midpoint Theorem and its converse, a triangle's area scaled by a factor of 2 (ex12-2-5b, ex12-2-6a/b/c), and angle-sum arithmetic, not parallelogram properties as such. The description names only parallelogram properties plus congruent triangles. This may be a mapping issue between the objective and its question set.

Book abbreviations seen in the canonical reasons: 'opp sides of ∥m', 'opp ∠s of ∥m', 'alt ∠s', 'corresp ∠s', '∠s opp equal sides', 'Midpt Theorem', 'converse of Midpt Theorem', 'parm eq'. 'Parm eq' in ex12-1-4 style reasons and the Midpoint Theorem naming were not used in any entry because I wrote none. Also, ex12-1-6c has a minor working slip in the recorded text ('R = 292/2' where the line before is 68 + 2R = 360); the final answer 105 is consistent.
